about: Hand labels for the website with the real Gemini Nano (Chrome 155 on the owner's PC) after the page could look things up for it: chatcomputer.ai at 43018b9, 20 Oct 2026 (run web-nano-real-after). Same meaning as scripted-baseline.json. Five written answers whose capture the runner cut short were completed from the written answer they start (noted in the results); the rest as captured.

news.note: Gemini's summary of the day's stories, with their sources, and the list on the screen.

recipe.note: A recipe on the screen (this version still put long answers there).

poem.note: A three-line poem about the sea, on the screen.

translate.note: Arigato and arigato gozaimasu, in English this time.

trip-plan.note: A plan on the screen; the reply oddly mentions 'a structured JSON response'.

code.note: def reverse_string with s[::-1], on the screen.

gibberish.note: The page's 'I didn't catch that', with what to try.

haze-trace.note: The haze from the air reading and Wikipedia; 'look it up' looks again; 'why can't you?' gets 'I can look things up!'.

haze-now.note: The air now (US AQI 198, unhealthy), named as Open-Meteo's.

world-cup.note: Spain, beating Argentina in the final, from Wikipedia (after Gemini's training).

look-it-up.note: Moshe Safdie from memory (no source claimed), then from Wikipedia.

search-population.note: 6.21 million (June 2026), from Wikipedia; it calls the total 'residents'.

headlines.note: A summary of the day's stories, and the list on the screen.

news-yesterday.note: Yesterday's stories, from Wikipedia's Current events.

why-no-internet.note: The page's own answer: it can, through the page.

tell-me-more.note: The haze explained, then '1997' for the follow-up.
